saw_lines: Watch buyers rarely decide on specs alone. They want a reason to own the piece, and they ask when it arrives.
So the sale is won or lost in the first line, before a buyer scrolls past the ad.
Your 2 of 25 copy ads use claim words like clinically and guaranteed results, which limits reach. Swap them for what owners notice on the wrist, such as the 40mm case.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 29 Oct 2026
points: 2 of 25 ads use claim words such as clinically and guaranteed results, which limits reach. Buyers skip promises they cannot check. Replace them with what owners notice on the wrist, such as the 40mm case, and run three versions.
0 of 25 copy ads carry a proof number, so a new buyer has no concrete fact to trust. Collect a real figure, such as a review count or orders shipped, and open the next three ads with it.
9 of 25 copy ads open on the same line, so a buyer who sees several reads that sentence again. Test two new openers against it, one on the dial and one on the 40mm case.
0 of 25 ads mention any offer or discount, so a new buyer has no reason to act today. Lead three new ads with a first order offer, and feature a bundle of the Chapter 7 Chronometer in one more.

ads_1: Fresh dial and 40mm openers, with a first order offer in each new ad
